Method of Attack: Ransomware as a Service (RaaS) using ransomware written in Javascript
Encrypts victim's data using AES encryption targeting specific file extensions
Uses NW.js platform to create cross-platform ransomware executable
Distributes ransomware via affiliate program requiring only a bitcoin address
Creates persistence via shortcut in Startup folder
Communicates with TOR Command and Control server
Displays ransom lock screen demanding bitcoin payment
Impacted Systems: potentially Linux and Mac (due to NW.js cross-platform capability)
Attack Vector: Affiliate distribution of customized ransomware executable
Self-extracting archive executed on victim machine
Indicators of Compromise: Shortcut named ChromeService.lnk in Startup folder
Files such as ffmpegsumo.dll, g (settings file), msgbox.vbs, nw.pak, rundll32.exe (renamed TOR executable), s.exe (renamed Shortcut.exe from OptimumX), u.vbs
Ransom lock screen displaying ransom note in English or Spanish
Bitcoin address used for ransom payment
TOR affiliate service URL (underground TOR site)
